odm/etc/selinux/odm_seapp_contexts
# NOTE: odm/etc/selinux/odm_sepolicy.cil and the stock precompiled_sepolicy* are
# intentionally NOT extracted. They are platform-policy-version 33.0 artefacts
# (*_33_0 type aliases, resolved by /system/etc/selinux/mapping/33.0.cil), while
# this build's platform policy is 202504 and /vendor/etc/selinux/plat_sepolicy_vers.txt
# is generated as 202504. First-stage init therefore compiles sepolicy itself with
# mapping/202504.cil, and including the 33.0 odm policy makes secilc fail
# ("Failed to resolve typeattributeset statement at /odm/etc/selinux/odm_sepolicy.cil:2")
# which makes init LOG(FATAL) "Unable to open SELinux policy" and reboot to the
# bootloader before the boot animation. odm policy is optional to init.
#
# NOTE: /odm still carries the precompiled_sepolicy that this build generates, and
# first-stage init loads that binary policy in preference to
# /vendor/etc/selinux/vendor_sepolicy.cil (system/core/init/selinux.cpp,
# FindPrecompiledSplitPolicy prefers /odm/etc/selinux/precompiled_sepolicy and only
# falls back to compiling the CILs when no precompiled policy exists). A device
# sepolicy change is therefore only in effect after odmimage is rebuilt and
# odm.img is flashed (or a full OTA is applied); flashing vendor.img alone leaves
# the kernel running the previous policy and the new rules silently do nothing.
odm/etc/vintf/manifest_p19ae.xml
odm/etc/vintf/manifest_p19ap.xml
# NOTE: the weaver AIDL manifest is intentionally NOT extracted.
#
# /odm is the stock Xiaomi image: its weaver service (odm/bin/hw/android.hardware.weaver,
# started by odm/etc/init/android.hardware.weaver.rc) only ever ran under the stock ODM
# policy, which this build does not ship, so the binary is never started here. The
# declaration alone is enough to break boot: ServiceManager.isDeclared() returns true for
# android.hardware.weaver.IWeaver, LockSettingsService.onThirdPartyAppsStarted() calls
# waitForDeclaredService() while holding the ActivityManagerService lock, servicemanager
# retries the lazy start forever (the rc never advertises the weaver interface anyway), and
# 67 s later the watchdog kills system_server:
#
#   main: SyntheticPasswordManager.getWeaverAidlService -> ServiceManager.waitForServiceNative
#         LockSettingsService.migrateUserToSpWithBoundKeysLocked -> SystemServer.startOtherServices
#
# Without the manifest fragment the framework logs "Device does not support weaver" and falls
# back to gatekeeper-only synthetic passwords, which is how a weaver-less device boots.
#odm/etc/vintf/manifest/android.hardware.weaver.xml
odm/etc/vintf/manifest/manifest_vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.mtdservice.xml

# toolbox_vendor and toybox_vendor, so /vendor/bin already gets both binaries and

# rest from toybox). Shipping the stock ones as well made the vendor image
# claim those paths twice, which soong rejects as a packaging conflict.

# NOT extracted: the stock wpa_supplicant/hostapd are linked against the
# firmware's OpenSSL 1.1 (undefined symbol sk_dup), which this ROM does not
# ship -- only BoringSSL, which has no sk_dup. Exec then fails with
#   CANNOT LINK EXECUTABLE "/vendor/bin/hw/wpa_supplicant": cannot locate symbol "sk_dup"

vendor/lib/libboot_control_qti.so
# libbluetooth_audio_session_aidl.so is built from
# hardware/interfaces/bluetooth/audio/utils (aidl_session). The stock copy is
# from the Android 15 vendor and predates GetLeAudioOffloadCodecInfo(), which
# android.hardware.bluetooth.audio-impl references, so loading the AIDL BT audio
# HAL dies with "cannot locate symbol …GetLeAudioOffloadCodecInfo…". That HAL
# never registers IBluetoothAudioProviderFactory/default, and com.android.bluetooth
# blocks in BluetoothAudioHalVersionManager::Get() waiting for it, which is why
# the adapter stays in TURNING_ON/OFF and never scans. Keep the built one.
